summary: **For Petitioner** : Shri V.C. Sekhar, PGCIL Shri Amit Garg, PGCIL Shri Ranjeet Kumar Pandey, PGCIL **For Respondents** : None The Petitioner, Power Grid Corporation of India Limited (PGCIL), has filed the instant - _“1) Admit the capital cost as claimed in the Petition and approve the Additional Capitalisation incurred / projected to be incurred._ - _4) Allow the petitioner to recover the shortfall or refund the excess Annual Fixed Charges, on account of Return on Equity due to a change in applicable Minimum Alternate/Corporate Income Tax rate as per the Income Tax Act, 1961 (as amended from time to time) of the respective financial year directly without making any application before the Commission as provided in Tariff Regulation 2019 as per para 8 above for respective block._ - _5) Approve the reimbursement of expenditure by the beneficiaries towards petition filing fee, and expenditure on the publishing of notices in newspapers in terms of Regulation 70 (1) Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2019, and other expenditure (if any) in relation to the filing of the petition._ - _6) Allow the petitioner to bill and recover Licensee fees and RLDC fees and charges, separately from the respondents in terms of Regulation 70 (3) and (4) Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2019._ - _7) Allow the Petitioner to claim the overall security expenses and consequential IOWC on that security expenses separately._ - _8) Allow the petitioner to claim the capital spares at the end of tariff block as per actual._ _and pass such other relief as Hon’ble Commission deems fit and appropriate under the circumstances of the case and in the interest of justice.”_ 8. The Respondents, mainly beneficiaries of the Northern Region, are Distribution Licensees, Generation Utility and Power Departments, which are procuring transmission services from the Petitioner. 9. The Petitioner has served a copy of the Petition on the Respondents, and notice regarding the filing of this Petition has also been published in newspapers in accordance with Section 64 of the Electricity Act, 2003 (hereinafter referred to as “the Act”). No comments or suggestions have been received from the general public in response to the notice published in newspapers by the Petitioner. None of the Respondents has filed their reply. 10. The first hearing in the matter took place on 18.11.2024, and the final hearing was held on 23.1.2025, during which the order was reserved. This order is issued considering the submissions made by the Petitioner in the Petition and the Petitioner’s affidavits dated 28.2.2024, 9.12.2024 and 12.9.2024. 11. Having heard the Petitioner’s representatives and having perused the material on record, we proceed to dispose of the Petition. 16. We have considered the Petitioner’s submissions. After taking into consideration the _# Petitioner has sought condonation for 41 days; however, the actual delay is 42 days._ 34. The detailed justification for the delays provided by the Petitioner is as follows: 41. The Petitioner has stated that the IA was accorded on 27.03.2022 with a schedule of 14 months, and the LOA was issued on 4.5.2022 and 19.5.2022, respectively. Subsequently, the Petitioner, with its project implementation expertise and experience, made every effort to complete the transmission scheme, which was commissioned on 12.7.2023. It is clear that the delay was beyond the Petitioner's control, and even the events causing the delay were unforeseen, although various issues related to securing the shutdown contributed to the delay in the transmission scheme. 42. In compliance with the query of the Commission vide RoP for the hearing dated 18.11.2024, the Petitioner in its affidavit dated 9.12.2024, has reiterated the submissions made earlier and requested to condone the delay in the completion of the transmission assets on the grounds that it was beyond the control of the Petitioner. _# The Petitioner has sought condonation for 41 days, however actual delay is 42 days._ 44. The Petitioner has provided a detailed justification for the delay in commissioning the transmission assets. We have considered the Petitioner's submissions, and the detailed analysis of the delay regarding the transmission assets is as follows: 51. Furthermore, regarding the delay caused by the deferment of shutdown, we have considered the documents on record and found that the shutdown requested by the Petitioner _*The last date of the month has been considered, as the exact date has not been mentioned. # The Petitioner has sought condonation of the delay of 41 days; however, the actual delay is 42 days._ 56. The Petitioner has claimed IDC and submitted the statement showing the IDC claim and discharge of IDC liability as on COD regarding the transmission assets as follows: 62. We have considered the Petitioner’s submissions. It is observed that the Petitioner - _(d) Liabilities to meet award of arbitration or for compliance of the directions or order of any statutory authority or order or decree of any court of law;_ 82. We have considered the Petitioner’s submissions, and it is observed that the Petitioner 87. The Petitioner has sought reimbursement of the fee paid by it for filing the Petition and publication expenses. The Petitioner shall be entitled to reimbursement of the filing fees and publication expenses in connection with the present Petition, directly from the beneficiaries on a pro-rata basis in accordance with Regulation 70(1) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations. 96. We have considered the Petitioner's submissions. Since we have determined the transmission tariff for the transmission assets in this order, the request for the interim tariff becomes redundant. 98. This order disposes of Petition No. 184/TT/2024 in terms of the above findings and discussions.
